extracted.intended_audience: FOIA requesters, DNFSB legal/FOIA staff, and members of the public who submit or defend FOIA requests
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards for submitting, processing, appealing, and protecting information under the Defense Nuclear Facilities Safety Board's proposed FOIA regulations (10 CFR part 1703). Includes definitions, fee rules, processing tracks, denial content, and privileged/confidential treatment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions — Designated FOIA Officer and Chief FOIA Officer duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated FOIA Officer serves as the Chief FOIA Officer and is the person designated by the Board to administer the Board's activities pursuant to the regulations in this part. The Designated FOIA Officer shall also be the Board officer having custody or responsibility for agency records and shall be the Board officer responsible for authorizing or denying production of records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adds responsibilities from the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016, including offering training to employees, serving as the primary liaison to the Office of Government Information Services and the Office of Information Policy, and membership on the Chief FOIA Officer Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods for FOIA requests
rubrics_metrics.description: FOIA requests may be addressed to the Designated FOIA Officer and submitted by mail, by email at FOIA@dnfsb.gov, or via the government-wide FOIA.gov portal. Requests should be clearly marked 'Freedom of Information Act Request.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amends prior rules that permitted only mail; instructs requesters how to address and label requests for proper processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for records available through the electronic reading room
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for agency records available through the electronic reading room include Board correspondence, except that which is exempt from mandatory public disclosure under §1704.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies which records are considered available through the electronic reading room and therefore subject to that provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Educational institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational institution refers to any school that operates a program of scholarly research and includes students who make a request in furtherance of their coursework or other school-sponsored activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expands definition to include student requests made for coursework/research, which may affect fee status and fee waivers under FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Representative of the news media
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative of the news media refers to any person or entity that gathers information of potential interest to a segment of the public, uses editorial skills to turn raw materials into a distinct work, and distributes that work to an audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes prior 'organized and operated' requirement and adopts OPEN Government Act definition; aligns with D.C. Circuit case law that broadened who may qualify for media fee status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee waiver/fee assessment when agency misses statutory deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will not assess search fees or duplication fees from educational and noncommercial scientific institutions if it has failed to meet the regulatory deadline in 1703.108.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conforms to OPEN Government Act and D.C. Circuit precedents limiting fees when agencies miss statutory timeframes; affects fee calculation and requester rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charging fees for 'unusual circumstances' where >5,000 pages are required
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board has determined that unusual circumstances apply and more than 5,000 pages are necessary to respond, the Board may charge search fees (or duplication fees for certain preferred-status requesters) provided it has: given timely written notice of unusual circumstances and discussed with the requester (or made at least three good-faith attempts) how to limit the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires timely notice and discussion of scope-limiting steps per 5 U.S.C. 552(a)(6)(B)(ii); provides process before imposing fees in large or complex requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court-determined 'exceptional circumstances' excuse for missed time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If a court determines that 'exceptional circumstances' exist as defined by FOIA, the Board's failure to comply with a time limit shall be excused for the period specified by the court order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits judicially-ordered excusal of agency time limits; distinguishes court-determined exceptional circumstances from agency unusual circumstances for fee assessment purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing order — first-in, first-out with misdirected requests rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board ordinarily will respond to requests according to their order of receipt. In instances involving misdirected requests, the response time will commence on the date that the request is first received by any Board office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes default processing order and clarifies when the statutory response time begins for misdirected submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multitrack processing (processing tracks)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will designate a specific track for requests granted expedited processing and may designate additional tracks that distinguish between simple and more complex requests based on estimated work or time needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors the Board may consider include number of pages and the need for consultations or referrals; the Board shall advise requesters of the track assigned and, when appropriate, offer an opportunity to narrow requests to move to a different track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregating requests for 'unusual circumstances' determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of satisfying unusual circumstances under FOIA, the Board may aggregate requests where it reasonably appears multiple requests by one requester or a group acting in concert constitute a single request; the Board shall not aggregate multiple requests that involve unrelated matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregation is limited to related or concerted requests and used only to determine if unusual circumstances apply for extensions/fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when determinations exceed statutory period and OGIS information
rubrics_metrics.description: If no determination has been made at the end of the ten-day period (or last extension), the requester may deem administrative remedies exhausted and seek judicial review. If the Board is unable to provide a response within the statutory period, the Designated FOIA Officer shall inform the requester of the reason for the delay, expected determination date, and may ask requester to forgo court action until determination; Board must also alert requesters to Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) dispute resolution services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances notice of exhaustion-of-remedies rights with a request to postpone litigation and explicitly directs disclosure of dispute resolution options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial letters — required content and signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Denial of a request shall be signed by the Designated FOIA Officer and include: (1) name and title/position of person denying; (2) a brief statement of reasons including any FOIA exemption applied; (3) an estimate of volume of records withheld (page count or other reasonable estimate), unless providing estimate would harm an interest protected by an exemption or deletions on disclosed records make estimate unnecessary; (4) a statement that the denial may be appealed and description of requirements under §1703.109; and (5) a statement notifying requester of FOIA Public Liaison assistance and OGIS dispute resolution services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardizes denial content to assist requesters in understanding reasons, scope of withholding, and appeal/dispute resolution options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal timing for fee waiver/fee reduction denials
rubrics_metrics.description: A person denied a fee waiver or reduction may appeal that determination to the General Counsel within 90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revises prior 30-day appeal window to the 90-day minimum required by the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal extension in unusual circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: In unusual circumstances as defined in §1703.108(f), time limits for deciding an appeal may be extended by up to ten working days by the General Counsel, who must send written notice setting forth reasons and expected determination date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links appeal extensions to the unusual-circumstances aggregation and multitrack framework; requires written notice for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privileged or confidential information — procedures to claim protection
rubrics_metrics.description: A person claiming information is privileged or confidential must file: (1) an application with an affidavit requesting privileged/confidential treatment stating justification; (2) the original document marked on the front page 'Contains Privileged or Confidential Information—Do Not Release' and identifying the information for which treatment is sought; (3) three copies of the redacted document with a statement indicating information removed for privileged/confidential treatment; and (4) contact name, title, address, telephone, and email for persons to be contacted regarding the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies documentary and procedural requirements for asserting Exemption 4-type confidentiality claims and requests careful labeling and redaction practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of documents while privilege/confidentiality claim is pending
rubrics_metrics.description: The Designated FOIA Officer shall place documents for which privileged or confidential treatment is sought in a nonpublic file while the request is pending. The request for privileged treatment and a copy of the redacted document shall be placed in a public file while the claim is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placing materials in a nonpublic file is not a determination on the claim; the Board retains discretion to make determinations and to release information as necessary to carry out responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and opportunity to comment for third-party submitters
rubrics_metrics.description: When a requester seeks a document for which privilege or confidentiality is claimed, the Designated FOIA Officer shall notify the person who submitted the document and give them an opportunity (at least five days) to comment in writing on the request; a copy of this notice shall be sent to the FOIA requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures third-party submitters have chance to justify confidentiality before disclosure and promotes procedural fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice before release when claim of privilege/confidentiality denied
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of a decision to deny a claim of privilege or confidentiality, in whole or in part, shall be given to the claimant no less than five days before public disclosure; the decision shall follow consultation with the General Counsel and briefly explain why objections were not sustained. A copy of the notice shall be sent to the FOIA requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides claimants time to seek judicial relief and requires explanation of denial reasoning to promote transparency; involves General Counsel review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of suit to submitter of confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: When a FOIA requester brings suit to compel disclosure of privileged or confidential information, the Board shall notify the person who submitted documents containing such confidential information of the suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures submitters are informed of litigation that may affect their confidentiality claims and allows them to intervene or respond as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Supreme Court precedent on Exemption 4 (Food Marketing Institute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Removes regulatory language requiring the agency to determine substantial harm to a competitive position of the owner of information when applying Exemption 4, to conform with Food Marketing Institute v. Argus Leader Media, 139 S. Ct. 2356 (2019), and adds the word 'confidential' in relevant paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Updates regulatory standard for exemption 4 to reflect Supreme Court holdings; alters how agencies assess trade secret/commercial/financial information claims under FOIA.
